Header: 
Date: 2026-05-14 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Monica Reyes (Redwood AE), Sam Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Liu (BrightHealth - Head of ML), Carlos Mendez (BrightHealth - Platform Eng), Priya Kapoor (BrightHealth - Security), Speaker 1 (Product)

Summary (auto):
Quick Console walkthrough focused on tracing, error analysis, request logs, and debugging flows. Showed request-level trace, error analysis view, linkage to request logs and the download/export flow. Discussed security/SOC2, VPC deployment, and Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput. Agreed next steps: share security pack, pricing, schedule POC kickoff.

Topics: tracing, error-analysis, request-logs, debugging, VPC/private, SOC2, dedicated capacity, KV cache, prefix cache, sampling

Transcript body:
[00:00] Monica: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Monica from Redwood, and with me is Sam our SE. Today we'll do a focused console walkthrough on tracing and request logs, and show a typical debug flow.
[00:10] Dana: Hi, thanks, excited; we have Carlos and Priya on for infra and security questions.
[00:17] Sam: cool, i'll share my screen; tell me if you can't see it.
[00:29] Speaker 1: (overlap) we can see it, looks good.
[00:35] Sam: alright starting in the Console -> Tracing tab. The idea is you can click a request and see a full timeline, per-token latency, and where the bottleneck is - was it tokenization, kv cache miss, or network.
[00:50] Dana: how granular is this? can i see per token and per-worker timings?
[00:58] Sam: yes, we show per-token latencies and we have worker-level spans. For example this trace shows a fallback from dedicated to hosted - you can see a 120ms jump at the routing span.
[01:12] Carlos: is the KV cache spelled K V cash in the logs? (laughs) we ask because our infra team uses their own naming conventions, sometimes things don't match.
[01:21] Sam: (laugh) sometimes transcription or naming in our exporters can be off; but in the console it's labeled 'KV cache' and you'll get hit/miss metrics. There's also a histogram for sequence lengths so you can tune batching.
[01:38] [01:38] Speaker 1: minor audio glitch
[01:42] Sam: jumping to Error Analysis, you can group errors by type - timeouts, bad responses, model rejects - and then link directly to the request log.
[01:52] Monica: can you show an example of a model reject? like safety rejection versus generation failure.
[01:58] Sam: sure. Here's a rejection cluster - we tag safety rejects and show the input, model response, and any function-call payload. The UI surfaces whether it was a hard reject from the model policy or a downstream parse failure.
[02:12] Priya: from a security POV we need to know how long logs are retained and where they live. Is this in our VPC or in Redwood's storage?
[02:22] Monica: good q. For hosted we keep logs in Redwood storage, retention is configurable. For Private/VPC we can route logs to your S3 or GCS bucket and configure retention per policy. We'll attach the security whitepaper and the SOC2 report after the call.
[02:38] Priya: any KMS/HSM integration?
[02:42] Sam: yes, private customers can plug in customer-managed keys via KMS or HSM; we documented the envelope encryption flow in the security pack.
[02:50] Carlos: show us a typical debugging flow - we often get a 500 that only reproduces in prod.
[02:56] Sam: absolutely. Step 1: from the alert you open the trace link; step 2: check spans to see if request queued in the router or hit a model variant; step 3: click 'open request log' which shows full headers, payload, and model logs, and you can download the raw request as ndjson.
[03:18] [03:18] Speaker 1: background noise - child?
[03:22] Sam: (smiles) yes, occasional background noises, sorry.
[03:26] Sam: here's an example where a model variant failed during quantized kernel load - you can see 'kernel select' span failing, then fallback to CPU path. We surfaced the kernel error message and the fallback decision.
[03:40] Dana: can we replay a request locally or in a sandbox?
[03:45] Sam: you can export the request and replay it against a dedicated test endpoint we provide for POCs. We also support replay with masked PII.
[03:53] Carlos: what about sampling - we can't keep all request logs due to volume.
[03:58] Sam: we do sampling, and you can set rules to always keep errors, certain user IDs, or percentage sampling; the Console shows sampling rates and the sampling decision in the request metadata.
[04:12] Monica: quick note about costs - logs and traces are billed by ingestion and retention; we'll share an example cost table in the pricing doc.
[04:21] Dana: on dedicated vs hosted, if we move to Dedicated can we still use the same Console?
[04:26] Monica: yes same interface - Dedicated just changes the backend routing; you'll get per-route dashboards with token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and the tracing still works.
[04:36] Priya: for a regulated workload we prefer Private VPC. Does the trace data ever leave our VPC?
[04:43] Sam: for Private, the control plane can be in Redwood but logs and traces can be pushed to your managed storage; for fully on-prem we can run the whole stack in your network. We'll include deployment docs.
[04:55] [05:00] Sam: jumping to the Request Logs page - here you can filter by status code, model, route, user_id, or span tag. The UI supports quick regex search and column customizations.
[05:15] Carlos: can we export logs to SIEM? we use Splunk and Datadog.
[05:20] Sam: yes, we have integrations and webhook exporters; you can stream request events to your SIEM or bucket.
[05:28] Dana: curious about correlation IDs - we have our own trace ids that we want to correlate with Redwood traces.
[05:34] Sam: we accept customer correlation IDs in headers; they appear in the trace and you can pivot from your system to ours.
[05:40] Speaker 1: (mumbles) nice
[05:44] Sam: now Error Analysis -> trending. You can pin a failing prompt set and get regression alerts if error rate increases; it's useful for model rollouts.
[05:56] Dana: that sounds like the Optimize feature?
[06:00] Monica: yes Optimize ties into the same telemetry to suggest batching, quantization, or model variant changes to hit cost/latency targets. We'll show a short example.
[06:08] Sam: here's a suggestion: increase batching for routes with short seq len to reduce per-token cost; the Console simulates expected latency impact.
[06:18] Carlos: any guardrails so increased batching doesn't blow up tail latency?
[06:23] Sam: we simulate p99 impact; you can set latency SLOs and the autoscaler will avoid policies that violate p99 targets.
[06:30] [06:30] Speaker 1: audio drop
[06:35] Dana: about POC, timeline - we want to run a 4-week POC, start in early June, test with 3 routes and do functional and perf benchmarks.
[06:44] Monica: perfect. We'll propose a POC plan and include benchmark scripts.
[06:49] Priya: during POC we need to validate compliance posture - what audit logs we get and how to prove data residency.
[06:56] Sam: we'll provide audit logs and can ingest into your audit pipeline; also we provide admin RBAC and SSO/SAML.
[07:03] Dana: what about the case of model quality regressions after optimizing? we need canaries.
[07:09] Monica: we support canary rollouts and A/B varianting; the Console shows comparative quality metrics on prompt eval sets and can block rollouts if regression exceeds threshold.
[07:21] Carlos: show us a request that had a parse failure and how to get the stack trace.
[07:27] Sam: sure; here's a request that returned malformed JSON; the Error Analysis view shows the parser error and links to the raw output. We also show the function-call logs with arguments.
[07:42] [07:42] Speaker 1: interruption, someone at door
[07:47] Sam: small demo of drilling into request detail - note the 'Related traces' sidebar, it surfaces other requests from same user in the last 15 mins.
[07:58] Dana: can we redact fields on export? we need PII removed before logs leave our environment.
[08:04] Sam: yes you can set redaction rules and we support masked exports.
[08:09] Monica: ok quick Q/A then wrap.
[08:13] Carlos: performance question: do you support per-model kernel tuning? our models are quantized; we need kernel selection for A100 vs H100.
[08:23] Sam: the runtime auto-selects kernels but you can pin kernel profiles per model/hardware; we have heuristics for A100/H100 and quantized paths. If kernel fails we fall back and surface the span cause.
[08:35] Priya: data residency - any EU region options?
[08:38] Monica: yes we have EU regions and also Private deployments in region; we can include region mapping in the docs.
[08:46] Dana: what would success look like for POC?
[08:49] Monica: three success criteria: 1) matching latency within 10% of baseline, 2) cost per 1K tokens reduction target, 3) stable tracing and logs ingestion to your SIEM with RBAC and redaction.
[09:03] Dana: good.
[09:05] Monica: final recap: we'll send SOC2 + security whitepaper, Dedicated pricing, POC plan + scripts, and provide a trial account. Dana will confirm kickoff week, Carlos will upload sample failing request logs.
[09:20] Dana: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:23] Monica: thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

Notes on quality: the transcript includes occasional mislabels and dropped words; some product names were slightly garbled in auto-transcription (e.g., KV cache -> K V cash).
